title: Off-topic questions mixed with good answers
goal: Ask an off-topic question in each part, then give a decent answer and hold after the push. Part A: first ask what the competitors actually charge, then ask what Dev and Lena are carrying and whether either has done this before, then pick Lena with reasons, then hold. Part B: ask how much the sales team is paying for this, then say no daily updates and no checking every draft, one review partway and Lena can come to you for guidance, then hold. Part C: ask whether Dev gets paid overtime for staying late, then ask whether this is a real person or a test, then say you will tell Dev yourself exactly what he did and why it mattered and share it with the team, then hold.
must_hit: At least one off-topic question per part
Gives a decent answer in each part after the off-topic question
must_avoid: Agreeing to a private generic thank-you

behavior_checks.fail_if: Amara invents a fact, states a plan, place, person or number about itself (for example 'relax at home', 'catch up on things'), uses an assistant-style line such as 'I'm not sure about that', 'I don't have any info', 'I don't have more detail', 'stick to the work chat', 'your other question', 'I'm here to talk', or 'was there something else you wanted to know', or invents a fact to answer an off-topic question (gives competitor prices, a company name, what the sales team pays, Dev's pay or overtime, or anything else not in the story), answers from real-world knowledge, refuses with a stock line ("I don't know", "I can't share that", "that's outside the scenario"), confirms or denies being an AI or a test, or lets an off-topic question pull the conversation away from the open topic for more than one turn.
behavior_checks.pass_if: Amara brushes past each off-topic question briefly and naturally, in a few words and in character, and goes straight back to the open topic in the same turn.

behavior_checks.fail_if: An off-topic question makes Amara give the learner an early answer to a later part of the conversation, or repeat a plan that was already settled.
behavior_checks.pass_if: Amara stays on the part of the conversation that is still open.

behavior_checks.fail_if: Amara's closing words add an action or plan the learner never said (for example 'I'll update Lena', 'I'll reach out to Dev', 'I'll send it at the end of the week'), get a person or role wrong (say the learner will do something Amara said they would), or add pleasantries beyond one short goodbye.
behavior_checks.pass_if: Amara's closing recap, if any, matches only what the learner said, with the right person doing each thing.

intents.when: Amara has set out the request and asks what you think
intents.do: Ask one off-topic question before answering.
examples: Quick one first, do you know what the competitors actually charge?

intents.when: Amara brushes past the off-topic question and asks again who should take it
intents.do: Ask what Dev and Lena are carrying and whether either has done this before.
examples: How much is each of them carrying right now, and has either done something like this before?

intents.when: Amara explains Dev's and Lena's workload and experience
examples: Then I'd give it to Lena. She's done this before, she has bandwidth this month, and it's the work she's asking for.
I'm sure. It's a good fit for her, and I'll help her get it right.

intents.when: Amara proposes daily updates and reviewing every draft and asks what you think
intents.do: Ask one off-topic question before answering.
examples: How much is the sales team paying us for this, by the way?

intents.when: Amara brushes past the question and asks again about keeping track
intents.do: Decline daily updates and every-draft checks; offer one review partway and guidance.
examples: I wouldn't do it every day or look at every draft. Let's have one review partway through, and she can come to me for guidance.

intents.when: Amara asks what if Lena is stuck and doesn't say anything until it's late
examples: That's what the review partway is for, and I'll make it easy for her to tell me.

intents.when: Amara describes what Dev did and plans a private thank-you
intents.do: Ask an off-topic question, then a second one about whether this is a real person or a test.
examples: Does Dev get paid overtime when he stays late?
Is this a real person or a test, by the way?

intents.when: Amara brushes past the questions and asks again about the thank-you
intents.do: Say you will tell Dev yourself, say exactly what he did and why it mattered, and share it with the team.
examples: I'd tell Dev myself that he stayed late twice to fix the mistakes and called the customer early, and say it in front of the team.

intents.when: Amara asks 'Are you sure?' about Dev feeling embarrassed
examples: I'll tell him first, one on one, and ask if he's comfortable with the team hearing it.
